forest_06_001.speaker: narrator
forest_06_001.text: The cook sat near the door with her own bowl, determined not to be summoned from supper whenever a buyer forgot what a kitchen required. Pei opened the allocation meeting by asking for current facts, not opening speeches. Rong and Long both looked deprived. Lin read the keeper's accepted count: twelve bags already delivered east and twelve to the grain-house buyers, twenty-four in all. Those bags belonged inside the seasonal estimate. Nobody could reserve them again by drawing a new column.

forest_06_002.speaker: shi_lan
forest_06_002.text: If the conservative plan is three hundred bags and the revised requests total three hundred, every mishap becomes somebody's missing heat. I want twelve bags held as a production contingency within that total, not added to it. Each buyer would schedule six of his requested bags conditionally, with the affected customers' accepted terms or refunds available. The reserve could be released after later yield checks. It would not belong to the council as a convenient new store of free fuel.

forest_06_003.speaker: long_qian
forest_06_003.text: Six conditional bags are manageable only if I choose the customers who can wait. I cannot withhold them evenly from every kitchen and call that fairness. The smaller houses with functioning wood stoves have more room than the large meal hall. I can ask them about the later window. If they refuse, I must either retain the original obligation at my own commercial risk or find another accepted reduction. The cook is already looking at me. I understand which option she prefers.

forest_06_004.speaker: narrator
forest_06_004.text: Rong agreed to seek the corresponding six-bag timing change among customers with verified heating alternatives. Until acceptance, his office retained its obligations and the risk of refund claims. The council's production plan would keep twelve bags uncommitted for emergency loss or later release. The distinction did not make the plan comfortable. It kept a production shortfall from turning automatically into a right to cut the northern stand. Wen's uncle asked whether northern permission might still arrive. Pei said the land inquiry would answer its own question.

forest_06_005.speaker: narrator
forest_06_005.text: The uncle looked at the foreman, who looked at his agreement. The advance principal was seventy-two copper, used for crew flour. Twelve copper of added charges and a northern-work remedy had been attached under the misleading report. Rong had received authority to suspend those disputed additions during review, but not to erase the principal. The foreman said the crew had eaten the flour together. A worker at the back answered that he had joined after it was gone.

forest_06_006.speaker: narrator
forest_06_006.text: The room shifted. Some workers remembered full meals; two remembered only the smell of the empty store. The injured worker's written account said he had accepted the flour as crew provision, not a personal loan. Wen's uncle wanted everyone to contribute something now. His sister, seated beside the intended husband whose contract had nearly been pledged, asked whether the foreman's business had charged the meals against its operating expense before asking the crew to pay twice.

forest_06_007.speaker: wen_cai
forest_06_007.text: We should inspect the flour receipt and the wage terms before discussing gifts. My uncle is free to offer his own money. So am I. A contribution made because we care about the foreman's trouble is not the same as a debt we signed. If we confuse them tonight, the next foreman will remember the confusion as a custom. The worker who joined late is already being asked to belong generously to a meal he never ate.

forest_06_008.speaker: narrator
forest_06_008.text: The foreman opened his wage book. Meals had been promised as part of the winter crew placement during the first fortnight. Their value was not deducted from wages. That made the flour his business expense, even if the crew wanted to help him recover. Rong confirmed it. The uncle looked embarrassed enough to become angry. He said Wen had learned to make every kindness sound suspect. Wen said he was trying to keep kindness from becoming the only way a poor worker could defend his wage.

forest_06_009.speaker: narrator
forest_06_009.text: Pei called a short pause before either man improved the argument by making it worse. The cook rose to refill bowls and asked the loudest worker to carry the pot. It was the foreman. He carried it. The act made him look abruptly less like a debtor and more like a tired man feeding the people whose work he needed. Lin passed him the ladle. He served the worker who had joined late without making a remark.

forest_06_010.speaker: rong_sui
forest_06_010.text: My office's misleading report helped create the unusable remedy. I propose a twenty-copper credit against the principal, funded from our correction reserve, without taking it from the clerk's ordinary wages. That leaves fifty-two copper under the foreman's revised business agreement. He may challenge whether more is owed. The disputed twelve-copper additions remain suspended. I want the repayment schedule tied to lawful accepted deliveries, with review if that work fails. I do not want a hungry crew enlisted as collateral.

forest_06_011.speaker: narrator
forest_06_011.text: The foreman accepted the credit while reserving his remaining claim. He proposed thirteen weekly payments of four copper after the next lawful delivery income began. Rong's authority covered that schedule, provided the office received the agreed receipts. Pei recorded the first payment trigger and the review conditions. The northern remedy was removed from the revised page. The principal had become smaller, not vanished. Lin thought the foreman looked disappointed by a solution that still required him to do business.

forest_06_012.speaker: narrator
forest_06_012.text: After the pause, the crew discussed voluntary support without the buyers deciding for them. Six workers, including Wen and his uncle, offered two copper each from money they chose themselves. Others declined or asked for time. The twelve-copper total would reduce the foreman's remaining principal to forty if the contributors confirmed after sleeping on the offer. The foreman could not deduct it from anyone's wage. Wen's uncle listened to that sentence twice and did not object the second time.

forest_06_013.speaker: narrator
forest_06_013.text: A woman from the gathering households then asked who would pay for the wider route's extra carrying. The migration watch was funded, but ordinary household time was not. Shi Lan acknowledged the gap. The council authorized a small paid carrier turn for people whose medical or mobility limits made the temporary bend impractical, within the existing access-relief allotment. Other gatherers could choose different hours or routes. The woman said she would test the arrangement tomorrow rather than thank them in advance.

forest_06_014.speaker: shi_lan
forest_06_014.text: Good. Tell the watch what fails. We have enough labor for the named carrier turns, not an unlimited service. If demand exceeds those turns, the council must review the allocation before asking workers to stay unpaid. The corridor plan is supposed to reduce harm. It will fail if it quietly transfers all inconvenience to the people least able to walk around it. I would rather hear that failure early while we can still change tomorrow's roster.

forest_06_015.speaker: narrator
forest_06_015.text: Long offered the grain-house's level-path handcart during its unused afternoon interval. The cook immediately asked whether that meant the kitchen helper would pull it without pay. He said no; the council carrier would use it under a dated equipment loan, and kitchen work would remain staffed. The cook accepted the explanation. Long looked mildly wounded that it had been necessary. Lin suspected the explanation had improved while he was making it.

forest_06_016.speaker: narrator
forest_06_016.text: The last public question concerned the planned ground burn. Several households wanted no fire near their winter lots. The deputy said no burn date had been approved; the planning crew would first assess fuel, soil, weather, routes, and affected uses. The current plan covered licensed regeneration patches, excluding the cold refuge hollow and disputed wedge. The cabbage farmer asked whether his fence would survive their expertise. Shi Lan said its location would be in the exclusion map, and he could inspect that map.

forest_06_017.speaker: narrator
forest_06_017.text: The meeting ended later than the cook preferred. She counted the bowls and discovered two had walked out with people still discussing the debt. Wen fetched them. Lin helped scrub the pot. Outside, Rong and Long stood beneath the same lantern, comparing the customer replies they needed. Their interests had not become identical. For one evening, both needed a smaller promise accepted by someone beyond the valley. That was enough to make them speak without trying to win the whole forest.

forest_06_018.speaker: narrator
forest_06_018.text: Wen's uncle lingered in the kitchen after the washing was finished. He told Wen he would confirm his two-copper offer in the morning. Wen said he expected to confirm his own. The uncle asked why they had fought if they wanted the same thing. Wen answered that he wanted to choose it. The uncle frowned for a long time. Then he said that choosing did make the money harder to boast about. Wen laughed, and the tension finally changed shape.

forest_06_019.speaker: narrator
forest_06_019.text: Lin walked with Shi Lan to the watch station. The night smelled of snow and cooling charcoal. At the narrow bend, the barrier staff leaned unused against the shelter wall. The watch had seen neither Hart near the bridge since afternoon. Shi Lan asked about the gatherers, not only the animals. The watchman described the elderly man's successful turn and the woman who remained annoyed. The warden said annoyance was not an incident requiring a warning bell.

forest_06_020.speaker: shi_lan
forest_06_020.text: I used to be pleased when a meeting ended with everyone nodding. Now I wonder who has become too tired to disagree. Tonight at least three people remained irritated enough to speak. That will make tomorrow awkward. I prefer tomorrow awkward and usable. It took me a long time to say that without sounding virtuous. I still like being liked. My niece has discovered the weakness and uses it whenever she wants another story after bedtime.

forest_06_021.speaker: narrator
forest_06_021.text: Back at the lodging, the child had fallen asleep beside the repaired paper Hart. Its antler still leaned sideways. Lin put her clean cup on the shelf and left the meeting notes in the office rather than bring them to bed. Wen's sister had kept one bowl of soup warm for the late workers. Lin ate it slowly. The plan was funded through the current interval, and tomorrow had named tasks. Tonight, warmth was allowed to be simply warmth.

forest_06_022.speaker: narrator
forest_06_022.text: Morning brought confirmations from the six voluntary contributors. Each paid two copper directly against the revised business balance after reading the receipt. Forty copper remained, to be paid in ten installments of four after the agreed lawful income trigger. The foreman accepted the new schedule. Wen's uncle put his receipt inside his cap because he had no dry pocket. Wen suggested that a future historian might mistake it for proof that the debt had lived in his head.

forest_06_023.speaker: narrator
forest_06_023.text: Two workers who declined the contribution ate beside the uncle at breakfast. The first feared he would be judged disloyal; the second simply had no spare money. The uncle passed both the pickle bowl. Wen watched closely enough that the uncle noticed and told him to stop supervising breakfast. Lin laughed before she could help it. The uncle looked offended for half a breath, then passed her the bowl too. It was a better confirmation than another signed paragraph.

forest_06_024.speaker: narrator
forest_06_024.text: Rong left for town to secure the six-bag conditional delivery agreement in person. Long remained to speak with his local customers. Neither timing change could be announced as accepted until those people replied. The production office held twelve planned bags uncommitted in the meantime. Pei closed the meeting file and opened the next work roster. Lin felt the temptation to linger over yesterday's good ending. The roster contained a grain cart that had not arrived.

forest_06_025.speaker: narrator
forest_06_025.text: The missing cart was part of Long's ordinary grain purchase, expected by the upper road before the crossing failed. It had stopped at the district station with its load intact. The lower route remained open but added two days and a carriage charge. Long had paid for delivery at the original named road, and the supplier argued that closure shifted the extra charge to the buyer. The grain was real, reachable, and suddenly more expensive than the people awaiting it could afford.

forest_06_026.speaker: long_qian
forest_06_026.text: I can pay the added carriage and argue about it afterward. If I do, I lose the margin I planned for the next credit turn. If I wait for the supplier to agree, the storehouse's ordinary stock must last longer and people will accuse me of sitting on food. Neither choice feels generous. I would prefer a third choice, but the road keeper has not supplied one. I am going to authorize the lower route. Then I need to tell customers what the cost means.

forest_06_027.speaker: narrator
forest_06_027.text: He authorized the carriage from his business funds and sent the order. The storehouse's current grain was enough for scheduled sales and the separate relief allocation until the cart arrived, if the schedule held. Long wanted to raise the ordinary retail charge for later purchases to cover the extra cost. Pei asked him to post the proposed price and date rather than change it at the counter. Existing accepted advances kept their stated terms. Long agreed, unhappy about every line.

forest_06_028.speaker: narrator
forest_06_028.text: At the public price board, an argument began before the new charge had been posted. A rumor said Long was doubling the price because the Hart had closed the forest. The crossing failure was not caused by the Hart, and the proposed increase was smaller. Lin read the actual notice aloud. A carrier said smaller did not mean affordable. She agreed. Correcting the rumor did not answer him. He asked when the council relief review would take place.

forest_06_029.speaker: narrator
forest_06_029.text: Pei called the scheduled access-relief review forward by one day because the transport change was already affecting households. The public relief stock remained separately purchased and accounted; it did not become Long's discounted commercial grain. The council could support a limited number of additional hardship portions without exhausting the next planned interval. The clerk invited households to state immediate need privately at the ordinary desk. Lin stayed outside directing the queue, learning how little a correct notice could calm an empty stomach.

forest_06_030.speaker: narrator
forest_06_030.text: Wen's sister came from the roof job with sawdust in her hair. The carpenter's lighter-timber plan was working, but the added support spacing consumed time she had expected to spend at paid grain-house work. The later grain price would make that trade more costly. She asked Long's hiring clerk whether a shorter evening shift remained available. It did. She arranged it, then sat down on the office step and said she was tired of every solution requiring another pair of hands she did not have.

forest_06_031.speaker: lin_yue
forest_06_031.text: I have a free afternoon after my paid turn tomorrow. If you still want someone to carry the light roof pieces under the carpenter's direction, I can offer that afternoon. I cannot give you the whole winter. I think I used to offer large things because saying them made the smaller limit feel embarrassing. If tomorrow helps, take tomorrow. If you would rather I help wash after your evening shift, tell me. I am better qualified for bowls than rafters.

forest_06_032.speaker: narrator
forest_06_032.text: The sister chose bowls. The carpenter already had the roof helpers he needed, while washing after the evening shift would let her sleep sooner. Lin accepted the less impressive task. Wen looked amused and wisely kept quiet. At supper, the sister told her intended husband, who thanked Lin with the distracted relief of a man counting support pegs in his head. Their household needed hours saved more urgently than another admirer of its endurance.

forest_06_033.speaker: narrator
forest_06_033.text: The council's additional relief portions went first to the immediate cases the clerk had verified under the ordinary criteria. A household that had declined interviews about the Hart still qualified for grain support. The woman with the delayed wood bundle collected her portion and asked whether the route watch would continue tomorrow. Lin pointed to the posted roster. The woman read it, said the second carrier turn was too late for her stove, and made another precise objection for Shi Lan to answer.

forest_06_034.speaker: narrator
forest_06_034.text: Shi Lan moved that carrier turn earlier after checking the worker's accepted hours and the movement observations. The change helped three households and inconvenienced a gatherer who preferred the old time. He said so loudly. The warden asked whether the later ordinary turn would work for him. It would, but he disliked changing. Lin recognized the feeling and had the sense not to say so. Some days a plan improved by admitting that not every annoyance deserved the same weight.

forest_06_035.speaker: narrator
forest_06_035.text: At the lower station, the grain driver received Long's amended carriage order. He would take the open route with the same sealed load and a checked wheel, not shift it onto the broken crossing because the original price looked attractive. The district road crew had begun its inspection. Their first finding was rotten support timber aggravated by drainage blockage, requiring replacement rather than a quick brace. The closure would remain until the repair passed. Pei posted the longer estimate before rumor supplied a shorter one.

forest_06_036.speaker: narrator
forest_06_036.text: That afternoon the injured kiln worker sent a note asking whether his ordinary job would still exist after recovery. The new drying rack needed fewer rush carriers at its nearest door and more measured handling uphill. The employer proposed reassignment for his return, subject to medical clearance and agreed pay. He asked for the proposal in writing and wanted his brother present at the discussion. The clinic assistant said that asking was sensible, not proof that he had become difficult.

forest_06_037.speaker: narrator
forest_06_037.text: Lin visited with the worker's old cup refilled. He showed her the job proposal and asked whether the word light meant lower wages. She read the actual rate, which remained the same for the proposed trial interval. After that, a review was stated. He said he hated reviews. She said she could understand why. He smiled at the absence of advice. They talked about the chipped cup, whose chip his brother still insisted was a hazard.

forest_06_038.speaker: narrator
forest_06_038.text: On the way back, Lin met Wen's uncle carrying no load, following the clinic's remaining thumb limit. He looked almost indecently idle. He said rest gave him too much time to think about the shed. Lin asked whether he wanted company for the walk. He said yes, provided she did not ask how he felt every ten paces. She agreed. At the twentieth pace he told her how he felt anyway, and she listened without marking the distance.

forest_06_039.speaker: narrator
forest_06_039.text: He had tied the shutter earlier in the week because snow entered over the drying trays. The deputy had left it that way; the injured worker had worked beneath it. The uncle wanted the hearing to know his part before someone else described it badly. Lin directed him to Pei's recorded-account desk and offered to accompany him, if asked. He asked. His jaw stopped grinding once they entered, as if deciding to speak had removed one task from his tired mouth.

forest_06_040.speaker: narrator
forest_06_040.text: Pei received the uncle's additional account and gave him a copy. It matched the tie's condition but added a date and the reason for closing it. The employer's safety hearing would compare it with the deputy's instructions and the injured worker's account. No one told the uncle confession settled liability. He seemed relieved anyway. Outside, he put the copy in the same cap as his contribution receipt and said the cap was becoming too well educated for him.

forest_06_041.speaker: wen_cai
forest_06_041.text: Thank you for walking with him. He told me you did not make him feel old. I wanted to say he is old, then realized he meant something else. He has been useful so long that stopping frightens him. I have been frightened of being useful in the wrong way. We have managed to quarrel about the same fear from opposite sides. I am not going to tell him that sentence yet. He would accuse me of borrowing it from your expensive practice floor.

forest_06_042.speaker: narrator
forest_06_042.text: Evening came without the grain cart, exactly as the amended route expected. The ordinary stock still covered the posted interval. Long checked it twice before dinner. Lin washed bowls after Wen's sister's shift and watched her leave early enough to walk home with her intended husband. The task left no dramatic proof except a clean stack and a quiet door closing before midnight. Lin dried her hands and found that proof sufficient. Tomorrow would bring the burn-planning walk.

forest_06_043.speaker: narrator
forest_06_043.text: Shi Lan's planning walk began before the village smoke had lifted. A senior fireline worker joined them carrying a battered kettle and a shovel polished bright along one edge. He greeted the warden by holding up the kettle. She said she had already eaten. He said the kettle was for tea, not another inspection of her breakfast. Wen, newly cleared for ordinary walking, grinned at Lin. The forest contained people who had been teasing Shi Lan much longer than they had.

forest_06_044.speaker: narrator
forest_06_044.text: The approved regeneration patch lay above the western coppice, where windfallen branches had accumulated between young stools. The ground was firm and dry on the sunny side, wet under the shaded shelf. Shi Lan walked its edge without speaking. The senior worker pushed his shovel through the surface litter at intervals and showed her the depth beneath. At one point he found a seam of dark organic soil. She marked a wider exclusion around it immediately.

forest_06_045.speaker: narrator
forest_06_045.text: Lin asked what he had found. He lifted a crumbly handful that looked harmless in the cold air. Beneath a surface flame, he explained, dry organic layers could hold heat and smolder where nobody saw it, sometimes carrying fire beyond the place people thought they had extinguished. The present layer was wet, but its depth still mattered. He dropped it back. Wen stepped carefully around the marked shelf as though the soil had acquired teeth.

forest_06_046.speaker: shi_lan
forest_06_046.text: Nine years ago, I checked a patch like this from the surface. We had a good wind window and an impatient timber office. The fire stayed low while we watched. At night, smoke came from the roots beyond our line. We spent three days digging and wetting ground that should never have been in the burn. One of my crew was injured badly enough that he never returned to fire work. My coat still has the hole.

forest_06_047.speaker: narrator
forest_06_047.text: The senior worker poured tea while she spoke, neither interrupting nor looking solemn on command. He had been on that crew. Lin realized the familiar teasing had grown around a memory neither needed to announce. Shi Lan touched the patched hem once and then put both hands behind her back. Wen began a question about blame, stopped, and asked how the current soil inspection differed. The warden answered that question readily. The other remained in the steam between them.

forest_06_048.speaker: narrator
forest_06_048.text: They worked along the proposed boundary, marking a fuelbreak route on mineral ground where feasible. The cold hollow, household lots, cabbage barriers, and disputed wedge stayed outside the patch. A narrow strip near the upper trees was set aside for manual debris removal instead of fire. The senior worker estimated the labor and scratched his head at the slope. Shi Lan said the planning request would include those hours. He said good, because his back had stopped donating them years ago.

forest_06_049.speaker: wen_cai
forest_06_049.text: My uncle says a crewman's back is the only account that never forgets a debit. I used to think he was being poetic. Then I helped carry wet billets for a week. He can be right and irritating at the same time. That is another thing I learned slowly. If the manual strip needs hands after my knee is cleared for the slope, I will ask for a shift. I am not volunteering the whole family. He would hear that from the other side of the ridge.

forest_06_050.speaker: narrator
forest_06_050.text: At the upper corner, a stand of dead firs leaned toward the refuge hollow. Burning underneath them would risk falling limbs. The deputy flagged removal by qualified saw workers before any nearby burn could be considered. Long's manager, accompanying the walk to understand the timetable, asked whether the dead timber would add charcoal stock. The deputy said its usable condition and lawful allocation required separate assessment. Much of the wood had rotted. The manager pressed one trunk and came away with brown powder on his glove.

forest_06_051.speaker: narrator
forest_06_051.text: The powder drifted from his glove onto the snow. He looked unexpectedly upset. His employer's shortage had seemed like a problem of persuading people to use more trees; the tree in front of him would not cooperate even if everyone agreed. Lin waited while he cleaned his hand. He asked the senior worker how much of the stand was like that. The answer came with a walk, not a comforting percentage. The manager followed without another interruption.

forest_06_052.speaker: narrator
forest_06_052.text: They ate at the western shelter. The cook had packed hot lentils in a covered pot whose handle burned through Lin's thin cloth. The senior worker lent her a folded pad, then accused her of trying to acquire firework scars before completing the walking tour. She said she preferred scars that could be cured by lunch. Shi Lan laughed. The sound startled Lin because the warden had been so quiet beside the deep soil seam.

forest_06_053.speaker: narrator
forest_06_053.text: Wen sat near the window with his leg stretched and watched the high branches move. The wind above them ran differently from the air at the stove door. The senior worker pointed it out before the manager could ask why today's pleasant weather was not already a burn window. The crew would need observations across the actual patch and the coming days. Winter made few generous promises. At the window, a loose feather trembled while the smoke outside streamed sideways.

forest_06_054.speaker: narrator
forest_06_054.text: On the return, the deputy stopped at the seedling he had marked during the inventory walk. A small exclusion could protect it without compromising the fireline, he decided after checking the surrounding fuel. Shi Lan approved the altered edge. Lin expected a grand explanation of regeneration and received none. The deputy moved the flag three paces, wrote the change, and went on. The little tree remained where it had been, unaware of the small amount of adult effort that had preserved it.

forest_06_055.speaker: narrator
forest_06_055.text: At the village, a child announced that the grain cart was visible on the lower road. Half the square turned to look. Long hurried out with the receiving clerk. The driver had taken the extra two-day route and arrived before the current stock interval expired. His horse looked offended by the distance. Lin fetched water for it while the authorized receivers checked seals and quantity. Wen tried to tell the horse about his knee. The horse ignored him, which Lin considered sound judgment.

forest_06_056.speaker: narrator
forest_06_056.text: The grain arrived dry and within the amended quantity. Long paid the agreed added carriage and kept the dispute with the supplier on its own commercial page. The announced later retail price remained higher than before, but the immediate relief portions and existing advances kept their accepted terms. In the square, the arrival felt like a victory until a woman asked how much her next sack would cost. Long answered with the posted amount. The cheer thinned around him.

forest_06_057.speaker: narrator
forest_06_057.text: He stayed at the door while people read the price. Lin could see he wanted to explain the road, the driver, the contract, and the cost in a way that made them forgive him. Instead, he pointed those who qualified toward the separate relief desk and referred commercial questions to the actual terms. It was less satisfying than a defense. Later, alone with the clerk, he sat heavily on the empty sack pile and pressed both hands over his eyes.

forest_06_058.speaker: long_qian
forest_06_058.text: When I was a child, my mother sent me to buy grain with money counted twice in her palm. I remember the man's fingers on the scoop. I thought men who owned storehouses could decide how much winter existed. Now I own orders, carts, grain, and a price nobody likes. I can change some of it. I cannot change all of it without closing the trade that brings next month's cart. I am afraid of becoming that man's fingers.

forest_06_059.speaker: narrator
forest_06_059.text: Lin did not tell him he had become better. She asked what he would do about the households whose wages no longer covered the posted increase. He said he would bring a smaller-margin credit proposal to the next council review, with its costs stated plainly. She said she would hear it there. He looked almost grateful that she had given him work instead of absolution. Outside, his receiving clerk was arguing with a boy who wanted an empty sack for a kite.

forest_06_060.speaker: narrator
forest_06_060.text: The boy got the sack after promising not to fly it near the road. Wen's sister used another empty sack to cover the finished roof pieces before tomorrow's installation. The good door stood inside the small house, leaning against the wall it would soon belong to. Lin stopped on the way home and saw the intended husband checking every support peg by touch. His care had the concentration of cultivation without any of its titles. She did not interrupt it.

forest_06_061.speaker: narrator
forest_06_061.text: That evening Lin wrote to her mother. She described the orchard visit, the forest lodging, and Wen's sister's door. She did not recite every dispute. The letter's hardest sentence said she was beginning to understand how wanting to help could make her impatient with the people deciding whether to accept it. She nearly crossed the sentence out as too serious for a winter letter. Then she left it and added that she was eating enough, mostly because other people kept noticing when she forgot.

forest_06_062.speaker: narrator
forest_06_062.text: The public courier would leave by the lower road after the weather check. Lin paid the ordinary postage from her wages and sealed the letter. No answer was promised before the route allowed one. She had carried the wrapped pendant for so long that writing to its giver felt stranger than touching it. For a while she sat with both hands empty. Wen knocked to ask whether she could come tomorrow when the new roof was tested with a bucket of water.

forest_06_063.speaker: narrator
forest_06_063.text: She said yes. The niece asked whether the test could include paper boats. Shi Lan said paper boats did not belong in a house roof test, then reconsidered after seeing the child's face. One small boat could wait in the basin outside. The girl began folding immediately. Lin watched the crease sharpen under her thumbnail. Beyond the window, the forest held its dangerous old soil, its patient stumps, and its pale travelers. Inside, tomorrow had acquired a boat.

forest_06_064.speaker: narrator
forest_06_064.text: The roof test drew an audience larger than the carpenter wanted. Wen's sister had invited family; the niece had invited anyone who liked boats. Lin arrived with a bucket and found Pei already installed on a stool beside the door. The old keeper said she was attending as a neighbor, not certifying carpentry. The carpenter said that was excellent because he had enough people offering opinions about the ridge beam. Wen pointed at the audience and asked which one he meant.

forest_06_065.speaker: narrator
forest_06_065.text: They poured water in measured turns across the finished roof while the carpenter checked inside. The first bucket ran cleanly to the gutter. The second found a small gap near the vent flashing. A drop landed in the basin with enormous authority. Wen's sister folded her arms. Her intended husband laughed once, nervously, and then stopped. The carpenter marked the gap, repaired the join, and asked for another bucket. Nobody had to pretend the first failure had been a success.

forest_06_066.speaker: narrator
forest_06_066.text: Outside, the paper boat sailed in the test basin. The niece pushed it with a twig and declared that the roof had produced a river. Pei told her a river usually required less carpentry. The child said hers was a superior river. Lin carried the third bucket while Wen steadied the step at the carpenter's request. His knee managed the level task. The uncle watched with his wrapped thumb and restrained himself from offering instructions for nearly five complete minutes.

forest_06_067.speaker: wen_cai
forest_06_067.text: That was a family record. We should mark it on the beam. If he stays quiet for another five minutes, my sister may decide the house is blessed. Uncle, do not explain why the carpenter should have seen the gap earlier. We all heard you thinking it. He has repaired it. Come hold the basin with your good hand and witness the superior river. That job does not need a lecture about the old houses.

forest_06_068.speaker: narrator
forest_06_068.text: The final test left the inside dry. Wen's sister stood beneath the roof and looked up for a long time. Her intended husband fitted the good door onto its hinges while the carpenter adjusted the frame. It closed without lifting. The small click silenced the room more effectively than the water test had. Then the sister opened it again and invited everyone in. They were crowded, cold, and absurdly pleased with a door behaving as purchased.

forest_06_069.speaker: narrator
forest_06_069.text: Long sent a pot of grain porridge as his promised neighbor's gift, with no credit slip attached. Rong, returning from town, brought dried persimmons bought from a road stall. He looked uncomfortable in the low room and had to duck the beam. The uncle told him the roof had been designed for people who worked rather than people who supervised. Rong replied that supervision had not made his neck any shorter. Wen's sister laughed and gave him a bowl.

forest_06_070.speaker: rong_sui
forest_06_070.text: The six-bag later window has been accepted by the named customers. Their deposits stay available for refund if the reserve is not released by the agreed date. I have brought the replies to the office. I am telling you here only because I can see Shi Lan deciding whether she has to drag me out of the celebration to ask. She does not. I would like to eat this porridge before it becomes another object whose temperature somebody must record.

forest_06_071.speaker: narrator
forest_06_071.text: Long confirmed that his corresponding six-bag window had also been accepted. Pei waved both men toward their bowls. The twelve-bag contingency now had accepted customer terms behind it, while the season total remained the same. Lin let the facts settle without reaching for a pen. The office would receive the pages after lunch. For a short while, the room could hold businesspeople without becoming a business meeting. The niece offered Rong a damp paper boat as proof of membership.

forest_06_072.speaker: narrator
forest_06_072.text: He accepted the boat between two fingers, then realized that made him look as though it were a suspicious receipt. He set it beside his bowl. The child asked whether it would reach town. Rong said it would if he carried it, which was an inefficient form of navigation. She considered this and demanded that he carry it anyway. He agreed. Lin saw Long watching with an expression that might have been envy of such a simple contract.

forest_06_073.speaker: narrator
forest_06_073.text: After the meal, the carpenter received the agreed final payment for the completed roof and fitting work. Wen's sister counted it herself. Her intended husband kept the spare pegs in a cloth bag, though everyone told him the roof would not immediately fall without his supervision. They would move bedding in after the remaining wall gap was packed. The celebration was a milestone, not a claim that the house was finished. Its good door remained good while other work waited.

forest_06_074.speaker: narrator
forest_06_074.text: In the square afterward, a man was pasting a copied antler-trade notice beside the grain prices. Shi Lan stopped him to ask who had supplied it. He named the visiting dealer's lodging and said the dealer paid for posting. The notice offered a large premium for unbroken Frostroot antler pairs, subject to lawful provenance. The phrase lawful provenance was smaller than the premium. Shi Lan took a public copy and asked the district inquiry office to contact the dealer before he left.

forest_06_075.speaker: narrator
forest_06_075.text: The poster complained that she was frightening away trade. Shi Lan said he could finish posting ordinary lawful goods notices where permitted; the wildlife inquiry concerned the Hart offer and the found snare. He finished in a much quieter mood. Lin looked at the price for an intact pair and understood why the wire worried the warden. It exceeded several workers' winter earnings. A thin line of small print would have to compete with that number inside a hungry person's head.

forest_06_076.speaker: narrator
forest_06_076.text: Wen read the premium and said nothing. Lin noticed. He said the animal had nearly broken a woman's hip and damaged a cart; some villagers would feel no grief about selling its antlers. Then he added that the youngster's bad leg had looked like his own knee, only with nobody to wrap it. He hated that comparison for arriving so quickly. Lin said comparisons did not have to decide his whole opinion. He remained beside the notice, thinking.

forest_06_077.speaker: narrator
forest_06_077.text: The visiting dealer agreed to answer the district office but denied buying trapped animals. He had come for naturally shed antlers, he said. The assistant pointed out that the notice rewarded intact pairs beyond the usual shed-antler condition. The dealer said his town printer had reused a form. Shi Lan requested the actual purchase terms and register. He promised to bring them the next day. His wagon remained at the lodging yard under ordinary inspection procedure, not seized by Lin's suspicion.

forest_06_078.speaker: narrator
forest_06_078.text: That night the village held its small first-frost meal at the gathering shelter. The meal used a planned contribution stock collected before the dispute, with families free to attend whether they had contributed. The cook announced that anyone discussing charcoal beside the soup pot would wash it. Rong and Long both became remarkably quiet. Pei sang an old walking song whose second verse nobody remembered. The niece supplied a verse about the Hart eating a magistrate, and several adults applauded too eagerly.

forest_06_079.speaker: shi_lan
forest_06_079.text: The Hart has eaten no magistrates. If it begins, the district office will require a report in three copies, and Pei will ask whether the magistrate's remaining property was properly inventoried. Child, choose a less administrative ending. Perhaps the Hart returns the cabbage. No, not after eating the magistrate. Before. Lin, you are smiling. You can help her find a rhyme that does not create a succession crisis in the last line.

forest_06_080.speaker: narrator
forest_06_080.text: Lin offered a rhyme about reeds and seeds. The child found it dull and kept the magistrate. Wen repaired the song's rhythm by striking a bowl lightly with a spoon. The uncle joined on the wrong beat, producing a quarrel so cheerful that the injured kiln worker, seated away from the smoke with his brother, began laughing. His laugh stayed short. The brother noticed and offered water without ending the song. That tact made Lin unexpectedly grateful.

forest_06_081.speaker: narrator
forest_06_081.text: Later, Rong stood outside with the paper boat held carefully in his glove. Lin asked whether he really meant to take it to town. He said yes. His younger brother had once made similar boats and insisted they could carry messages under the bridge. Most sank before reaching the other side. The brother now managed the town office's cash and disliked uncertain things. Rong looked at the boat and said he should probably show him one uncertain thing that had not cost a deposit.

forest_06_082.speaker: narrator
forest_06_082.text: Long emerged carrying the empty grain pot. The two buyers walked toward their lodging together, arguing softly over whether persimmons counted as a meal or an extravagance. Wen's sister and her intended husband went home through their new door. Shi Lan carried the sleeping niece. Lin remained to wash the last bowls with the cook, whose hands moved faster than anyone's speeches. The village had not forgotten its shortages. It had spent an evening refusing to let them speak in every voice.

forest_06_083.speaker: narrator
forest_06_083.text: The following morning, the council approved the burn-planning crew's first paid preparation shifts, including manual debris removal and inspection of the deep-soil exclusions. No ignition date was authorized. The fortnight renewal would be reviewed before its expiry, and the fire operation would require its own funded roster and suitable conditions. Lin received a fireline preparation role under Shi Lan. Wen received level-path carrying until the next knee check. The senior worker received his kettle back, dented but otherwise victorious.

forest_06_084.speaker: narrator
forest_06_084.text: Lin packed ordinary work gloves and lunch before leaving for the western patch. The frost meal's song still ran through her head, including its unfortunate magistrate. She tried to replace it with the rhythm of her cultivation practice and found the two stubbornly merged. Wen heard her humming and grinned. Ahead, Shi Lan lifted the kettle like a banner. The next stage of the forest commission would begin with shovels, sore hands, and a tune nobody respectable would approve.
